lines.speaker: e
lines.text: In September nineteen seventy-nine, an American spy satellite saw two flashes over an empty ocean.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: A blink, then a longer glow.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: That double flash is the signature of a nuclear bomb.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The satellite had seen it forty-one times before.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Every one was a confirmed nuclear test.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: This one came from near the Prince Edward Islands, far south of Africa.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: No ship reported it. No country claimed it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Air Force planes flew twenty-five sampling flights.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: A White House panel said probably not a bomb, maybe space dust.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: But in Australia, sheep were reported to carry traces of radioactive iodine.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Navy scientists said underwater microphones heard a matching blast.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: President Carter wrote in his diary that his scientists believed Israel did it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Neither country has ever admitted it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: So who lit up the ocean that night?
